Subject: RE: Observed tail-latency increase in EU for model vX-RT (post-quant deploy)

Investigation summary and proposed mitigation plan:

What we see: the quantization delta (quantA) reduced activation memory on GPU but changed attention kernel tiling for long sequences; that path introduces a pathological enzyme in KV cache warmup for sequences with many context windows (Helios uses long sessions). The result is periodic long-latency outliers when the KV warmup path hits a worst-case loop; not all machines hit it but enough to affect p95/p99. Evidence attached: quant-diff-summary.pdf and kv-cache-warmup.log.

Immediate mitigations (recommended order):
1) FAST: Pin Helios routing to prior variant rev-2028-04-28 (vX-RT-stable) for the Helios tenant only (expected rollback time ~8 min to shift weights and allow caches to repopulate). This has the lowest customer disruption and no cluster-wide revert.
2) MEDIUM: If pinting isn't sufficient, open a 25% staged diversion to vX-lite-fallback for 2 hours while we push a hotfix to quantA to avoid the KV warmup path.
3) LONG: Rework the attention tiling path and add a guard in the runtime to detect pathological warmup and fallback automatically.

Risk/cost tradeoffs: tenant pin avoids cluster-wide churn; staged diversion keeps progressive fidelity for Helios. Both can be implemented without draining the cluster or taking down the model.

Requesting these approvals before we act:
- Authorization to pin Helios traffic immediately to vX-RT-stable (tenant-only revert)
- Authorization to declare a provisional SLA exception window for the Helios account from action time for up to 6 hours while we remediate; we'll calculate credits later if needed.

If approved, I'll run the tenant pin and monitor telemetry. I'll also prepare a short root-cause sketch for customer communication.

Kim
